text:
Sarah B: Hey folks — day 4 of runtime onboarding. Trying to build from source (bazel build //runtime:server) and hitting a linker error I can't parse. Full linker snippet below, any quick guesses?

Sarah B: ```
/usr/bin/ld: bazel-out/k8-fastbuild/bin/runtime/_objs/server/main.o: in function `main':
main.cpp:(.text+0x123): undefined reference to `__cudaRegisterFatBinary'
/usr/bin/ld: bazel-out/k8-fastbuild/bin/runtime/_objs/server/main.o: undefined reference to `__cudaUnregisterFatBinary'
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
```

Junaid A: Welcome aboard! That usually smells like a mismatched libcudart/libcuda link or building with static cudart but missing the proper linking order. Which nvcc and driver versions are you on?

Sarah B: nvcc --version -> Cuda compilation tools, release 12.2, V12.2.91
Sarah B: nvidia-smi -> Driver Version: 535.54.03, Kernel Module: 535.54.03

Mike T: Two quick things to check: 1) Are you building inside a container that doesn't have the host libcuda visible? 2) Run ldd on the final binary to see which cuda libs it's pointing at. e.g. `ldd bazel-bin/runtime/server`

Sarah B: ran ldd, here's the relevant lines:```
libcuda.so.1 => /usr/local/cuda-12.2/compat/libcuda.so.1 (0x00007f...)
libcudart.so.12 => not found
```

Olivia P: Ah, libcudart missing is the problem. Bazel probably linked against libcudart.so.12 but the runtime only exposes compat libcuda. If you're in a container, we usually bind-mount /usr/local/cuda and /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 from the host.

Junaid A: Also check whether the build is using static cudart (libcudart_static.a) — that pulls in __cudaRegisterFatBinary symbols differently. Search the linker flags in your bazel rules for -lcudart_static or -lcudart and try switching to shared libcudart.

Sarah B: Bazel rule uses -lcudart_static currently. If I switch to shared, how do I make sure the runtime finds libcudart.so.12?

Mike T: Option A: install the cuda toolkit dev packages in the container (cuda-toolkit-12-2) so libcudart is present. Option B: mount the host /usr/local/cuda/lib64 and add it to LD_LIBRARY_PATH in your container. Also `sudo ldconfig` on host if you added new libs.

CI Bot: build //runtime:server failed for user sarahb at 1876543211 (see logs).

Olivia P: If you want to iterate faster, you can disable CUDA while you chase the link issue: set -DUSE_CUDA=OFF in your local build flags so unit tests and non-CUDA parts compile. Then re-enable once linking is fixed.

Sarah B: Trying mounting host libs now. Quick question — where do we record recommended container base images for runtime devs? I want to make sure my dev image matches infra.

Mike T: We keep base images in eng-runtime/images repo (ping @Eng Oncall if you can't access). For local dev use the `dev-cuda:12.2-ubuntu22.04` image. There's a README with mount points.

Eng Oncall: pinged — will share the image links and a quick checklist in this thread. Also happy to pair.

Sarah B: Ok mounting /usr/local/cuda and reinstalling libcudart from the toolkit fixed the missing symbol. Switching to shared cudart and rebuilding now. Huge thanks y'all — pairing with Mike in 10 to tidy up bazel flags. :thumbsup:
